title: Breaks or not sort and wudu helpdesk
subject: Islamic Studies
source: Written for islamic-studies/y3 lesson 16 (Pupil PDF worksheet: breaks or not sort and wudu helpdesk)
intro: Lesson 16: What breaks wudu, and the du'a after wudu. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

blocks.title: Sort into: Breaks wudu / Does not break wudu
blocks.task: sort them into the columns: Breaks wudu, Does not break wudu.
blocks.answer: Breaks wudu: Using the toilet; Deep sleep; Passing wind. Does not break wudu: Eating an apple; Laughing outside salah; Walking to the mat

passage.title: Taught by the Prophet ﷺ after wudu (Muslim)
paras: Ash-hadu an la ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah, wa ash-hadu anna Muhammadan 'abduhu wa rasuluh. (I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger.)

questions.q: Dear helpdesk, I used the toilet. Do I need wudu again?
questions.a: Yes: using the toilet breaks wudu, so make wudu again before salah.

questions.q: Dear helpdesk, I laughed at a joke (not in salah). Do I need wudu again?
questions.a: No: laughing outside salah does not break wudu.

questions.q: Dear helpdesk, I think I passed wind but I am not sure.
questions.a: Build on certainty: your wudu stays unless you are sure (a sound or a smell).

keywords.def: end: then we need a new wudu
bearing witness: there is no god but Allah

questions.q: Ali ate a sandwich after wudu. Does he need a new wudu? Explain.
questions.a: No: eating does not break wudu.

questions.q: Whose servant and Messenger is Muhammad ﷺ in the du'a?
Answer three 'Wudu helpdesk' questions on the pupil PDF: 1) I used the toilet; 2) I laughed at a joke; 3) I think I passed wind but I am not sure.
questions.a: 1) New wudu; 2) still has wudu; 3) still has wudu unless certain

questions.q: Extend: write the du'a's meaning in your own words.
questions.a: For example: Only Allah is God and Muhammad ﷺ is His Messenger.

questions.q: Stretch: why does Islam say a doubt does not break wudu?
questions.a: Islam is easy and stops us worrying; only certainty counts.

questions.q: Think again: what do you do if you are not sure your wudu broke?
questions.a: Stay with certainty: it has not broken.
